event: Environmental Monitoring Performance Qualification (EMPQ) results approved by QA prior to performing manufacturing operations in Building facility.
Closure Risk Assessment became effective to document operational details and environmental controls around unit operations in manufacturing facility.
Pfizer submitted BLA 125742/0 for COMIRNATY (BNT162b2) for active immunization to prevent COVID-19 in individuals ≥16 years of age.
EMA approved final protocol for study C4591021 (Post Conditional Approval Active Surveillance Study in Europe).
EUA Fact Sheets updated to include new Warning about myocarditis and pericarditis following post-authorization safety signal identification.
Investigation initiated to document deviation from protocol requirements when EMPQ was not executed with pre-approved protocol or summarized in final report.
Final protocol for pregnancy registry study (C4591022) submitted to FDA for review.
FDA Pre-License Inspection (PLI) of Pfizer Andover facility began for BLA STN 125742/0 review of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (COMIRNATY) drug substance manufacturing.
Drug substance batch placed on stability for product quality assessment following deviation related to control limit excursions during manufacturing.
Investigation initiated to document deviation regarding failure to perform required cleaning of equipment outside surfaces during specified timeframe.
FDA Pre-License Inspection of Pfizer Andover concluded; thirteen-item Form FDA 483 List of Inspectional Observations was issued to the firm.
EMPQ summary report written and approved following investigation into procedural deviations.
Investigation initiated for alarm condition observed within manufacturing area during biosafety cabinet operations.
Additional investigation initiated to document deviations regarding aseptic technique and insufficient work surface sanitization during observed operations.
FDA issued information request asking sponsor to propose postmarketing observational safety studies for myocarditis and pericarditis risk assessment.
Effectiveness check initiated to document effectiveness of bioburden mitigation strategy implemented per change control.
Pfizer submitted written response (Amendment STN 125742/0.25) outlining proposed corrective actions for all 13 inspectional observations.
Approximately 130 patients with post-COVID-19 vaccine myocarditis identified at Pediatric Heart Network sites for prospective registry enrollment.
FDA review memorandum concluded that proposed corrective actions for Observation Nos. 2-13 appear acceptable and may be evaluated during next routine inspection.
Sponsor's Internal Review Committee met to review reactogenicity and safety data for pregnant women RCT (C4591015) and recommended study continuation.
OBE/DE completed Pharmacovigilance Plan Review Memorandum (primary reviewer: Deborah Thompson, MD) for COMIRNATY BLA.
Sponsor responded to FDA Information Request regarding proposed myocarditis/pericarditis safety studies.
Protocol for study C4591021 submitted to FDA for review.
CBER Safety Working Group concurred with review team's proposed postmarketing requirements (PMRs) and commitments (PMCs) for myocarditis, pericarditis, and subclinical myocarditis studies.
Product Office memorandum from Anissa Cheung evaluated firm's response to Observation No. 1 regarding insufficient data supporting product quality and found it adequate.
Sponsor notified of PMRs/PMCs via FDA Information Request; pregnant women RCT had 259 subjects enrolled.
Pfizer submitted Amendment 46 (Seq 0046) containing COMIRNATY vial labels for Kalamazoo and Puurs manufacturing sites, and Hospira diluent sticker.

VAERS database queries conducted for adverse events of special interest: erythema multiforme (194 reports), glomerulonephritis/nephrotic syndrome (175 reports), and menstrual disorders (7,249 reports).
FDA CBER laboratory testing performed on COMIRNATY drug product to determine lipid nanoparticle size and polydispersity index (PDI) for three lots (FC3181, FC3184, FD0809) plus assay control.

Pfizer submitted Amendment 53 (Seq 0054) containing COMIRNATY carton labels (25 and 195 vial configurations) for both manufacturing sites, plus diluent vial and carton labels from Fresenius Kabi and Hospira.
Teleconference held between FDA and Pfizer to discuss firm's responses to Observation Nos. 2b, 2c, 6, and 9c from the FDA 483.
CDC data showed 201,577,973 doses of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine administered in the U.S.
FDA CBER sent email to Pfizer requesting consolidation of all draft carton and container labels into a single amendment for referencing in the Approval Letter for COMIRNATY BLA STN 125742/0.
Pfizer submitted additional updates and commitments via Amendment STN 125742/0.60 following the August 17 teleconference.
Pfizer submitted Dear HCP Letter as amendment 64 to the BLA for COMIRNATY (BLA STN 125742/0).
Pfizer provided FDA with list of seven launch lot numbers (FD7220, FE3592, FF2587, FF2588, FF2590, FF2593, FF8841) for COMIRNATY vaccine.
Pfizer confirmed no doses from the 7 launch lots had shipped yet; planned for September shipment with approximately one million doses remaining in Pfizer's control.
Pfizer provided FDA with list of lots in the field that comply with the BLA requirements.
FDA deadline for Pfizer to submit consolidated draft labels (by 12:00pm) for COMIRNATY BLA approval preparation.
Pfizer submitted revised carton and container labels for COMIRNATY BLA in amendment 63 (seq 0064).

CBER Product Testing Plan for COMIRNATY (COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine) established with effective date, establishing lot release requirements including protocol review and confirmatory CBER testing for BioNTech Manufacturing GmbH (License Number 2229, STN 125742).

COMIRNATY designated under Lot Release mode of regulation, requiring manufacturer to obtain lot-specific release from CBER before product distribution, with protocol review and confirmatory CBER testing selected as the release mechanism.

Initial version (Revision Level 01) of Product Testing Plan document created as a new document, establishing specifications for lot release protocol review including tests for filled vaccine and BNT162b2 drug substance.

CBER issued memorandum documenting in-support sterility and bacterial endotoxin test (BET) results for three lots (FC3181, FC3184, FD0809) of COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine COMIRNATY to support BLA approval STN 125742/0.
All three tested lots of COMIRNATY vaccine passed sterility testing (no growth of bacteria and fungi) by both CBER and Pfizer, meeting lot-release specifications.
Bacterial endotoxin testing results from CBER confirmed Pfizer's Certificate of Analysis values, with all conformance lots meeting proposed specifications.
Test memo issued documenting that CBER test results for lipid nanoparticle size and PDI are similar to BioNTech's firm results and meet proposed drug product specifications.
FDA CBER communicated that EUA-labeled lots in the field do not comply with the BLA since lot release activities have yet to be agreed upon and performed.
FDA stated they would develop a lot release approach with Pfizer after initial BLA approval occurs for COMIRNATY.
FDA instructed Pfizer to ensure EUA-labeled lots in the field are not listed on the cvdvaccine-us.com/resources website referenced in the Dear HCP Letter.
FDA CBER sent comment to Pfizer regarding vial labels for COMIRNATY (STN 125742/0), requesting additional diluent information and response by end of day.
Pfizer responded that additional diluent information proposed by CBER will not fit on vial label but is already included on carton label.
FDA acknowledged that diluent information will not fit on vial labels and confirmed Pfizer does not need to respond to the August 20, 2021 comment regarding vial labels.

CBER established Product Testing Plan for COMIRNATY (COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine) manufactured by BioNTech Manufacturing GmbH, documenting lot release requirements including protocol review and confirmatory CBER testing.
COMIRNATY received BLA License Number 2229 (STN 125742) with Product ID 2501 for active immunization to prevent COVID-19 in individuals 16 years of age and older.
CBER designated lot release mode requiring both protocol review and confirmatory CBER testing before manufacturer distribution, indicating enhanced regulatory oversight for this biological product.
Product Testing Plan approved by key CBER officials including Marion Gruber (Product Office Director), Jerry P. Weir (Product Division Director), and Maryna Eichelberger (Testing Division Director).
Sponsor committed to submit final study protocol for Pediatric Heart Network prospective cohort registry study with projected sample size and statistical analysis plan.
Sponsor anticipated completion of background troponin analysis for subclinical myocarditis assessment and enrollment of approximately 450 subjects in pregnant women RCT.
Action due date for FDA decision on BLA 125742/0 for COMIRNATY.
